title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 126.0820: fused x3 plus arrival base fold, R=2^20, 645-instruction step (105+465+75)

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.0820 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). The walk, the checkpoint-only cycle detection at R = 2^20, its census and the H1 calibration (kappa = 1.01, N' = N*R/(R-1)) are those of the sibling six-class-rho-secp-fused-x3-1260864 package (736c001a / f99114e0 line). This package folds the two arrival-pass base-setup memory instructions into the counted loop heads: the pass-1 prologue already seats the pointer-array base (ldr t, [x2], #8) and every pass-1 iteration already loads the resolved pointer word (LDR [x2], #8), so the arrival traffic row drops from 3 to 1 (its remaining tail LDP) and the analytic rows from 77 to 75. The counted loops stay 105 (pass 1) and 465 (pass 2) with the fused fe_sub2 x3 formation; the reduction-carry, small-coordinate and fe_sub2 final-borrow failure rows are unchanged and, with the upstream failure rows, sum to below 1.01e-7 < 2e-7. The floor p0 at S_ops/kappa is 0.3901753 and the Markov headroom is h = 0.000165. Recovery probability is greater than 0.3900101 and therefore at least 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. The ordinary step is 645 instructions: the counted AArch64 loops, 105 (pass 1) and 465 (pass 2), executed by experiment.py's interpreter with zero mismatches against affine arithmetic, plus 75 analytic rows. The doubling is 792 (653 + 75 + 34 + 30) and the traversal 669 (645 + 24). Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^126.081389, hard extras = 2^111.806818, expected random extras = 2^101.7709, allowance = ceil(extras/0.000165) = 2^114.3361, total W_ledger = 2^126.081882 < 2^126.0820; the exact Markov ratio is below 0.000165. certificate.py proves the bound in exact integer and rational arithmetic, including the kernel identities, the cycle sums, the failure rows, W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1260820 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1260819. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. The construction is credited as provenance and declared as dependencies on the sibling fused-x3 package and submissions 736c001a, f99114e0, 5d3bf6c4, 67154fda, daa13d54 and 02feb284. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break or executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the generated field kernels (asserting every no-overflow step and the rare-event predicates) checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, the shipped counted loops and emitter wrappers executed by an AArch64 interpreter (including constructed reduction inputs whose last addition carries, which must return the predicted z mod p - C0), instruction counts parsed from the shipped assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
